## The Sel1L-Hrd1 Endoplasmic Reticulum-Associated Degradation Complex Manages a Key Checkpoint in B Cell Development. 

Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) is a principal mechanism that targets ER-associated proteins for cytosolic proteasomal degradation. Here, our data demonstrate a critical role for the Sel1L-Hrd1 ubiquitin ligase complex in regulating this process and its influence on B cell lineage specification. Using a mouse genetic knockout/rescue model, we confirm that deficiency of Sel1L or Hrd1 components severely impairs early B cell differentiation, resulting in a reduced pool of immature/pro B cells and decreased levels of immunoglobulins. Mechanistic studies reveal that this defect stems from the requirement for efficient ERAD of certain pro-B cell transcription factors to properly maintain the expression and stability of other cell fate determinants.
